# Kudzu: full reference

> Kudzu is an open-source version control system for monorepos where most clients are AI agents and CI jobs. History, blame, diff, rebase and land run on the server. Clients fetch only the trees and blobs they ask for, through tiers of caches. Commits are changesets appended to a log, and refs move by compare-and-swap, so landing never takes a lock. This file is the complete CLI, MCP and HTTP API reference in one document.

Source: https://github.com/garyships/kudzu · Website: https://garyships.github.io/kudzu/ · Index: https://garyships.github.io/kudzu/llms.txt

## Concepts

- **Changeset**: the unit of work, an entry in the server's append-only log. It lists the files changed relative to its first parent (`mode: 0` means deleted). Its ID is the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON (64 hex characters). Creating one takes no lock and doesn't move any ref.
- **Ref**: a name such as `main` that points at a changeset. It moves by compare-and-swap.
- **Revision**: a ref name, a changeset ID or a unique hex prefix of at least 4 characters, optionally followed by git-style suffixes, applied left to right: `~N` for the Nth first-parent ancestor (`main~3`; `main~` is `main~1`) and `^N` for the Nth parent (`main^2` is a merge's second parent; `^` is `^1`). They chain: `main~2^2~1`.
- **Land**: put a changeset (and its unlanded ancestors) on a ref. The server rebases it onto the ref's current tip and compare-and-swaps the ref, retrying if it loses a race. There is no merge queue and no global lock. Overlapping edits fail with HTTP 409 and the conflicting paths. The three-way merge is conservative: adjacent edits count as a conflict too.
- **No push**: `kudzu commit` and `kudzu write` create the changeset on the server immediately.
- **Derived data**: root trees, per-path history (unodes), a first-parent skip list and blame are computed from changesets on the server. That is why `log PATH`, `blame` and ancestry checks are fast, and why none of them needs a checkout.
- **Tiers**: `kudzu server` (authoritative), `kudzu cache` (regional, in memory) and `kudzu daemon` (per machine, on disk, usually on a unix socket). All three answer the same object requests and forward `/api/*` to the server, so a client can point at any of them.
- **Working copy**: a directory with a `.kudzu/` folder. It holds the files of one revision (optionally sparse), a bounded object cache and an index. It never holds history.
- **Sparse (cone mode)**: a sparse directory includes everything below it, plus the files directly inside each of its ancestor directories (for example the root `README.md`). An empty spec means the full tree.
- **Remote address**: `host:port`, `http(s)://host:port` or `unix:///path/to.sock`. Resolution: `--remote` > `$KUDZU_REMOTE` > the working copy's recorded remote.
- **Author**: `--author "Name <email>"` > `$KUDZU_AUTHOR` > `user <user@host>`.
- **Token**: when the server runs with `--auth`, every client (CLI, MCP server, working copy, tier) sends `$KUDZU_TOKEN` as a bearer token. Tokens are never written to disk.

## Install and run

Quickest: one process runs all three tiers on top of a git repository.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garyships/kudzu/main/install.sh | sh   # or: go install github.com/garyships/kudzu/cmd/kudzu@latest (Go 1.24+)
cd /path/to/any/git/repo && kudzu up      # imports history, serves until Ctrl-C
export KUDZU_REMOTE=unix:///tmp/kudzu.sock   # in another shell
```

Each tier as its own process (how a real deployment runs):

```bash
kudzu import --store ./data --git /path/to/repo --as main     # git history -> changesets; re-run to add new commits
kudzu server --store ./data --listen 127.0.0.1:7070 &
kudzu cache  --upstream 127.0.0.1:7070 --listen 127.0.0.1:7071 &
kudzu daemon --upstream 127.0.0.1:7071 --listen unix:///tmp/kudzu.sock --dir /tmp/kudzu-objects &
export KUDZU_REMOTE=unix:///tmp/kudzu.sock
```

A single `kudzu server` is enough for experiments: point `KUDZU_REMOTE` at it directly.

## CLI

`kudzu <command> [flags] [args]`. Flags use Go syntax (`-n 5` or `--n 5`, not `-n5`) and may come before or after positional arguments. `kudzu <command> -h` lists a command's flags. Errors go to stderr with exit code 1.

### Infrastructure

| Command | Flags (default) | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `kudzu up` | `--git .`, `--ref HEAD`, `--as main`, `--dir` (per-repository folder in the user cache dir), `--port 7070` (cache on port+1; 0 picks free ports), `--socket /tmp/kudzu.sock`, `-v` | Playground: import a git repository (incrementally) and run server, regional cache and node daemon in one process until Ctrl-C. Refuses to start if the socket is in use. |
| `kudzu version` | | Print the version (`kudzu --version` works too). |
| `kudzu server` | `--store kudzu-data`, `--listen 127.0.0.1:7070` (host:port or unix:///path), `--mem 512MB`, `--lazy gen,unode` (derived types to compute on demand instead of eagerly), `--auth FILE` (access policy), `--meta postgres://…` and `--objects s3://bucket/prefix?endpoint=…` (shared backends instead of `--store`; `gs://` for GCS; credentials from `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`) | Authoritative server: SQLite metadata plus an object directory, or Postgres plus an S3-compatible bucket so several servers can serve one repository. With `--auth`, requests need a bearer token and per-directory rules apply (see Access control). |
| `kudzu token` | `--json` | Generate a random access token and the `token_sha256` to put in an `--auth` policy. |
| `kudzu cache` | `--listen 127.0.0.1:7071`, `--upstream 127.0.0.1:7070`, `--mem 1GB`, `--upstream-concurrency 32` | Regional in-memory object cache. |
| `kudzu daemon` | `--listen unix:///tmp/kudzu.sock`, `--upstream 127.0.0.1:7071`, `--dir $TMPDIR/kudzu-daemon`, `--max-disk 10GB`, `--upstream-concurrency 8`, `--seed FILE` | Per-machine on-disk object cache, shared by every job on the machine. |
| `kudzu import` | `--store kudzu-data` (or `--meta`/`--objects`), `--git .`, `--ref HEAD`, `--as main` | Import git history into a server store. Incremental: commits already imported are skipped. |
| `kudzu export` | `--store kudzu-data`, `--git PATH` (required), `--ref main`, `--as` (git branch, default same as `--ref`), `--force`, `--json` | Write the ref's history to a git repository (bare, or with the branch not checked out) and move the branch, fast-forward only unless `--force`. Incremental; imported commits map back to the originals, so exporting to the repository you imported from adds only what landed in Kudzu. |
| `kudzu snapshot` | `--remote`, `-r main`, `--sparse a,b`, `-o kudzu-seed.frames` | Save every object of a revision, for `kudzu daemon --seed`. |
| `kudzu stats` | `--remote` | Print a tier's statistics as JSON. |

### Queries (no working copy needed)

All take `--remote`. Inside a working copy, `-r` defaults to the checked-out changeset; elsewhere to `main`.

| Command | Flags | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `kudzu log [PATH]` | `-r REV`, `-n 20`, `--oneline`, `--json` | First-parent history, or the changesets that changed PATH (a file or a directory). |
| `kudzu blame PATH` | `-r REV`, `--json` | `<changeset> <author> <date> <line>) <text>` for each line. |
| `kudzu diff [PATH]` | `--from REV` (default: parent of `--to`), `--to REV`, `--merge-base`, `--stat`, `--json` | Unified diff, or `A/M/D path` lines with `--stat`. Inside a working copy with neither `--from` nor `--to`: your uncommitted changes. Outside one with neither: what `main` changed. `--merge-base` diffs from the common ancestor of `--from` and `--to`. |
| `kudzu show [REV]` | `--json` | Changeset header, `seq` and root tree, then `<mode> <blob> <path>` (or `D <path>`) for each change. |
| `kudzu cat PATH` | `-r REV` | Raw file content. |
| `kudzu ls [DIR]` | `-r REV`, `--json` | `<mode> <id> <name>`; directories end with `/`. |
| `kudzu refs` | `--json` | `<changeset> <name>` for each ref. |
| `kudzu merge-base A B` | `--json` | The merge base ID. Without `--json`, no common ancestor is an error; with it, `merge_base` is `""`. |

### Working copy

| Command | Flags | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `kudzu clone REMOTE DIR` | `-r main`, `--sparse dir1,dir2` | Create a working copy. DIR must be empty or missing. |
| `kudzu status` | `--json` | `M` modified, `D` deleted, `?` untracked (respects `.kudzuignore`: `name`, `dir/` and `path/glob` patterns). |
| `kudzu commit` | `-m MSG` (required), `-A` (add untracked files), `--land REF`, `--author`, `--json` | Upload missing blobs and create a changeset on the checked-out one; with `--land`, land it in the same call. If the land rebased, the checkout moves to the landed changeset. On a conflict nothing changes locally. |
| `kudzu land` | `--ref main`, `--json` | Land the checked-out changeset (and its unlanded ancestors), then move the checkout to what landed. |
| `kudzu rebase` | `-d main` | Rebase the checked-out stack onto `-d` on the server and move the checkout there. No ref moves. |
| `kudzu update [REV]` | `-r main`, `--force` | Move the checkout, rewriting only files that differ. Refuses if tracked files are modified unless `--force`, which discards local edits to tracked files (untracked files are kept). |
| `kudzu sparse` | `show` (default), `set DIRS…`, `add DIRS…`, `remove DIRS…` | Show or change the sparse directories (`set .` means a full checkout). Refuses while tracked files are modified. |
| `kudzu gc` | `--max-size 1GB`, `--json` | Trim the local object cache. |
| `kudzu gc --store DIR` | `--keep 30d`, `--dry-run`, `--json` | Server maintenance: remove changesets no ref reaches (older than `--keep`) and the objects only they used. Safe while the server runs. |

### Writing without a checkout

```
kudzu write [-r PARENT] -m MSG [--land REF] [--author A] [--delete PATH]... [--json] PATH=@LOCALFILE | PATH=@- ...
```

`-r` defaults to `main`. Each `PATH=@FILE` writes FILE's content to PATH in the repository; `@-` reads stdin. The executable bit comes from the local file. `--delete` is repeatable. Only blobs the server lacks are uploaded. Use the changeset you read the files at as `-r` (not a ref that may have moved), so changes landed since then are merged rather than overwritten.

### Agent integration

`kudzu mcp [--remote ADDR] [--read-only] [--author A]` serves the MCP tools on stdin/stdout (see below).

### Recipes

```bash
# history without a checkout
kudzu log -n 10 --oneline
kudzu log --oneline services/api
kudzu blame services/api/handler.go
kudzu diff --from main~5 --to main --stat

# sparse clone, edit, land
kudzu clone --sparse services/api "$KUDZU_REMOTE" wc && cd wc
kudzu commit -m "api: fix" --land main

# land rejected: "conflict in services/api/handler.go"
kudzu commit -m "api: fix"            # keep the change as changeset X (prints its id)
kudzu update -r main                  # clean checkout of the new main
kudzu diff --to X | patch -p1         # re-apply; clashing hunks land in *.rej (patch also leaves *.orig)
# resolve the *.rej hunks by hand, delete *.rej and *.orig
kudzu commit -m "api: fix" --land main

# API-only write, pinned to the revision that was read
REV=$(kudzu log -n 1 --json | jq -r '.[0].id')
kudzu cat -r "$REV" app.yaml > app.yaml && $EDITOR app.yaml
kudzu write -r "$REV" -m "config: tweak" --land main app.yaml=@app.yaml
```

## `--json` output

Supported by `log`, `blame`, `diff`, `show`, `ls`, `refs`, `merge-base`, `status`, `commit`, `land` and `write`. On success, exactly one JSON document goes to stdout. On failure, the exit code is 1 and stderr gets `{"error": "...", "status": <http status>, "conflicts": ["path", ...]}` (`status` and `conflicts` only when the server sent them).

- `log`, `blame`, `diff`, `show`, `ls`, `refs`, `merge-base`: the HTTP API response unchanged (see the HTTP API section).
- `diff` in a working copy without `--from`/`--to`: `{"files": [{"path": "a.go", "status": "M"}], "patch": "..."}`, tracked files only; `--stat` omits `patch`.
- `status`: `{"changeset": "<id>", "files": [{"path": "a.go", "status": "M"}]}`.
- `commit`: `{"id", "tree", "changes": <count>, "land": {"ref", "landed", "previous", "attempts", "rebased"}}` (`land` only with `--land`).
- `land`: `{"ref", "landed", "previous", "attempts", "rebased"}`. `landed == previous` means it was already on the ref.
- `write`: `{"id", "tree", "seq", "files": <changes>, "uploaded": <blobs sent>, "land": {...}}`.

## MCP server

`kudzu mcp` speaks the Model Context Protocol over stdio (newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0) and is built on the official Go SDK. It supports `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`, and sends server instructions that explain revisions and the write flow.

Flags: `--remote` (default `$KUDZU_REMOTE`, else the working copy in the current directory; it exits with an error if there is none), `--read-only` (register only the read tools), `--author` (default author for writes; default `$KUDZU_AUTHOR`, else user@host).

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add kudzu -e KUDZU_REMOTE=unix:///tmp/kudzu.sock -- kudzu mcp
```

Other clients (`mcpServers` JSON, e.g. Claude Desktop, Cursor):

```json
{"mcpServers": {"kudzu": {"command": "/usr/local/bin/kudzu", "args": ["mcp"], "env": {"KUDZU_REMOTE": "127.0.0.1:7070"}}}}
```

### Tools

Arguments marked `?` are optional. Read tools are annotated `readOnlyHint: true`. Write tools carry `destructiveHint: false`, except `kudzu_wc_update` (`true`). `--read-only` keeps only the read tools.

Read:

- `kudzu_resolve(rev)`: `{"rev", "changeset", "tree"}`. Use it to pin a moving ref.
- `kudzu_log(rev? = main, path?, limit? = 20, max 500)`: `{"rev", "head", "path"?, "more", "changesets": [{"id", "author", "date" (RFC 3339), "message", "parents", "change_count", "extra"?}]}`.
- `kudzu_blame(path, rev?, start_line?, end_line?)`: a JSON summary `{"path", "changeset", "total_lines", "start_line", "end_line", "truncated"}`, then a text block of `<changeset12> <author> <date> <line>) <text>` lines. At most 2000 lines per call.
- `kudzu_diff(to? = main, from? = first parent of to, merge_base?, path?, patch? = true, max_patch_bytes? = 102400, max 1048576)`: `{"from", "to", "files": [{"path", "status": "A"|"M"|"D", "old_mode"?, "new_mode"?}], "total_files", "patch_bytes", "patch_truncated", "note"?}`, then the unified diff as a second text block. Lists at most 1000 files.
- `kudzu_cat(path, rev?, start_line?, end_line?, max_bytes? = 102400, max 1048576)`: `{"path", "changeset", "mode", "type", "size", "binary", "truncated", ...}`, then the content as a second text block. Binary files (a NUL byte in the first 8000 bytes) are not returned. A directory is an error.
- `kudzu_ls(path? = root, rev?)`: `{"path", "changeset", "entries": [{"name", "type": "dir"|"file"|"executable"|"symlink"|"submodule"}]}`.
- `kudzu_show(rev)`: `{"changeset": {...as in log...}, "seq", "tree", "changes": [{"path", "mode"} | {"path", "deleted": true}]}`.
- `kudzu_ancestry(a, b)`: `{"a", "b", "merge_base", "a_is_ancestor_of_b", "b_is_ancestor_of_a"}`.
- `kudzu_refs(prefix?)`: `{"refs": [{"name", "changeset"}]}`.
- `kudzu_stats()`: the tier's `/stats`.
- `kudzu_wc_status(dir?)`: `{"root", "remote", "changeset", "sparse", "files": [{"path", "status"}]}` for a working copy on the MCP server's machine.

Write:

- `kudzu_write(parent, message, files?: [{path, content, executable?}], delete?: [path], land?, author?)`: creates a changeset on `parent` from inline UTF-8 contents, uploading only missing blobs, then lands it if `land` is set. Without `executable`, a rewritten file keeps its current mode. Returns `{"changeset", "tree", "parent", "files_written", "files_deleted", "blobs_uploaded", "land"?: {"ref", "landed", "previous", "rebased", "attempts", "already_landed"?}}`. Set `parent` to the changeset you read the files at.
- `kudzu_land(head, ref? = main)`: returns the land result as above.
- `kudzu_rebase(head, onto? = main)`: `{"head", "tree", "onto"}`. Creates new changesets and moves no ref.
- `kudzu_wc_commit(message, dir?, add_untracked?, land?, author?)`: `{"changeset", "tree", "changes", "now_at", "land"?}`.
- `kudzu_wc_update(dir?, rev? = main)`: `{"previous", "changeset", "tree"}`. Refuses if tracked files are modified, and never forces.

Errors are tool results with `isError: true`: invalid arguments, unknown revisions or paths, an unreachable server, `nothing to commit`. A conflict reads `conflict: <what happened>. Conflicting paths: a, b. <what to do next>`. A write whose land conflicts keeps its changeset (the message gives its ID) but doesn't land it. Calling a tool that `--read-only` hides is a protocol error (unknown tool).

## HTTP API

Served by `kudzu server`. Cache and daemon tiers forward `/api/*`, `/objects/missing` and `/objects/upload` to their upstream, and serve `/objects/*` from their own cache. Requests and responses are JSON unless noted. IDs are 64-character lowercase hex strings, and a zero ID is `""`. `rev` parameters accept any revision and default to `main`. Paths are repository-relative (leading and trailing `/` are ignored).

Errors: `{"error": "message"}` with status 400 (invalid request), 401 (missing or unknown token, when the server runs with `--auth`), 403 (`{"error": "permission denied: alice may not write docs/a.md", "path": "docs/a.md"}`; `path` is the denied path, or the ref for a land), 404 (unknown revision, path or object) or 500. Status 409 is a merge conflict, reported as `{"error": "conflict in a, b", "conflicts": ["a", "b"]}`, or a lost ref compare-and-swap (`{"error": "compare-and-swap conflict"}`).

File modes are decimal in JSON: 33188 (0100644 file), 33261 (0100755 executable), 40960 (0120000 symlink), 57344 (0160000 submodule), 16384 (040000 directory, in tree entries). A change with mode 0 deletes the path.

### Access control

`kudzu server --auth policy.json` requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request but `/healthz`. The policy maps token hashes to principals and principals to path-prefix rules:

```json
{
  "principals": {
    "alice": {"token_sha256": ["<from kudzu token>"], "read": [""], "write": ["services/api"], "deny": ["secrets"], "land": ["main", "users/alice/*"]},
    "cache": {"token_sha256": ["..."], "read": [""]}
  },
  "anonymous": {"read": ["docs"]}
}
```

The longest matching prefix decides (`""` is the whole repository; at equal length deny > write > read; write implies read). Reads (`cat`, `blame`, `ls`, `diff`, `log` with a path) need read access to the path; listings, diffs, change lists and the WAL leave out what the caller may not read, and a changeset that only touched such paths is hidden. Every changeset the server creates for the caller (create, rebase, merge, land) needs write access to each path it changes. Landing on or compare-and-swapping a ref needs a matching `land` entry. Uploading needs write access somewhere. Without `anonymous`, requests with no token get 401.

Objects are fetched by ID, so a caller with restricted read access only ever receives filtered trees: `/api/resolve`, `/api/changesets`, `/api/ls`, create, rebase, merge and snapshots return trees with unreadable entries removed (real tree objects, verified like any other). Clones and updates work unchanged; subtrees the caller may read in full keep their real IDs. Caches and daemons forward each client's token on `/api/*` and use their own `KUDZU_TOKEN` (normally a principal that reads everything) for upstream object fetches.

### Reading

- `GET /api/resolve?rev=` → `{"changeset", "tree"}`
- `GET /api/changesets/{rev}` → `{"id", "seq", "tree", "parents": [id], "author", "time" (unix seconds), "tz" (minutes east of UTC), "message", "changes": [{"path", "mode", "blob"}], "extra"?: {…}, "change_count"}`. `extra` holds e.g. `git` (the imported commit) or `rebased_from`.
- `GET /api/log?rev=&path=&limit=` → an array of changesets as above, without `changes`, `seq` or `tree` (`change_count` gives the number of changed files). First-parent history, or with `path` the changesets that changed that file or directory. `limit` defaults to 50, at most 10000.
- `GET /api/blame?rev=&path=` → `[{"line", "changeset", "text" (with its newline), "author", "time"}]`. 400 for directories and binary files.
- `GET /api/diff?to=&from=&merge_base=1&path=&patch=1` → `{"from", "to", "files": [{"path", "old"?: entry, "new"?: entry}], "patch"?}`. `from` defaults to the first parent of `to`. A missing `old` means added, a missing `new` means deleted. An entry is `{"name", "mode", "id"}`. `patch=1` adds a unified diff (`diff --kudzu a/P b/P` headers).
- `GET /api/cat?rev=&path=` → raw bytes, with headers `X-Kudzu-Mode` (octal) and `X-Kudzu-Blob`.
- `GET /api/ls?rev=&path=` → `[{"name", "mode", "id"}]`. A file path returns its own entry.
- `GET /api/ancestry?a=&b=` → `{"a", "b", "merge_base", "a_is_ancestor_of_b", "b_is_ancestor_of_a"}`
- `GET /api/refs` → `{"main": "<id>", ...}`
- `GET /api/wal?since=SEQ&limit=1000` → `[{"seq", "id", "parents", "author", "time", "tz", "message", "changes", "extra"?}]`, the log entries with `seq > since`, for indexers.
- `GET /api/snapshot?rev=&sparse=a,b` → a frame stream of every tree and blob of the revision, with header `X-Kudzu-Changeset`.
- `GET /stats` → server: `{"tier": "server", "uptime_seconds", "requests", "objects_served", "bytes_served", "changesets_created", "lands", "land_retries"}`. Cache or daemon: `{"tier", "uptime_seconds", "requests", "hits", "misses", "hit_rate", "coalesced_misses", "upstream_requests", "upstream_objects", "upstream_bytes", "upstream_failures", "objects_served", "bytes_served", "cached_objects"?, "cached_bytes"?}`.
- `GET /healthz` → `ok`

### Writing

- `POST /objects/missing` `{"ids": [id, ...]}` → `{"missing": [id, ...]}`. Ask before uploading.
- `POST /objects/upload`, a body of frames → `{"stored": n}`. Only blobs can be uploaded; trees and unodes are derived by the server, which verifies every hash.
- `POST /api/changesets` `{"parents": [id], "author", "message", "changes": [{"path", "mode", "blob"}], "time"?, "tz"?, "extra"?, "land"?: "main"}` → `{"id", "tree", "seq", "land"?: {"landed", "previous", "attempts", "rebased"}}`. Every blob must already be on the server. With `land`, a 409 means the changeset was created but not landed, and its ID is not returned (create first, then call `/api/land`, if you need it). `parents: []` creates a root changeset.
- `POST /api/land` `{"head": rev, "ref": "main"}` → `{"landed", "previous", "attempts", "rebased"}`. `landed == previous` means `head` was already on the ref.
- `POST /api/rebase` `{"head": rev, "onto": rev}` → `{"head", "tree"}`. No ref moves.
- `POST /api/merge` `{"ours": rev, "theirs": rev, "author", "message"}` → `{"id", "tree", "seq"}`, a two-parent changeset whose changes are listed relative to `ours`. No ref moves.
- `POST /api/refs/{name}` `{"old": id or "", "new": rev or ""}` → `{"name", "target"}`. Compare-and-swap: `old: ""` means the ref must not exist yet, and `new: ""` deletes it. 409 if the ref no longer points at `old`. Ref names may contain `/`.

### Object protocol

- Object ID: `sha256(kind + " " + decimal length + "\0" + content)`, where kind is `blob`, `tree`, `unode` or `changeset`.
- Stored form, identical on every tier and on the wire: one kind byte (`b`, `t`, `u`, `c`), one codec byte (0 raw, 1 zlib), then the payload. Blobs of 256 bytes or more are zlib-compressed when that is smaller.
- `GET /objects/{id}` → one stored object (`Cache-Control: immutable`).
- `POST /objects/fetch`: the body is concatenated raw 32-byte IDs (at most 65536). The response is a stream of frames.
- Frame: `id (32 bytes) | status (1 byte: 0 ok, 1 missing) | length (uint32 big-endian) | stored object`. A missing frame has length 0 and no payload. Streams can be resumed by asking again for whatever didn't arrive.
- Tree content: entries sorted by name, each `<octal mode> <name>\0<32-byte id>`.

### API-only write, step by step

1. `GET /api/resolve?rev=main` → parent changeset P (better: the changeset you read the files at).
2. For each new file content, compute the blob ID and stored form, `POST /objects/missing`, and upload the missing blobs as frames to `/objects/upload`.
3. `POST /api/changesets` with `parents: [P]` and the changes, and optionally `land`.
4. On 409, re-read the conflicting paths at the ref, redo the edit and write again.

`kudzu write` and the `kudzu_write` MCP tool do steps 1–3 for you.
